newsitem.title: USA: U.S. airlines to install cargo hold fire detectors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. airlines to install cargo hold fire detectors.

text.p: Major U.S. airlines agreed on Thursday to install fire detectors in the cargo holds of some 3,700 aircraft, a $400 million investment designed to increase airline safety after a string of crashes this year.

President Bill Clinton announced the plan after a White House meeting with 15 industry executives, including the chairmen of AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, UAL Corp.'s United Airlines and Delta Air Lines Inc.
"This is a critical part of our long range plan to make Americans more secure and to make sure our skies are safer," Clinton said.
A fire last May in the cargo hold of a ValuJet Inc airliner is believed to have caused a crash in the Florida Everglades that killed 110 people.

The White House has taken a high-profile interest in the issue of airline safety following that incident and the July crash of a Trans World Airlines airliner off Long Island, New York, that killed all 230 people on board.
Vice President Al Gore, who is chairing a commission on airline safety, said installing the fire detection equipment would begin next year and that it was expected to cost $400 million.
The airlines, who are bearing the cost, are making the installations voluntarily, he added.
"With this announcement, virtually all the airlines are saying that they're not going to wait for the regulatory process to catch up, they're moving forward on their own," Gore said.
